headline: 7 Critical Mistakes to Avoid When Planning a House Extension
articleBody:
Adding substantial square footage to your house should be an exciting upgrade, but simple oversights early on can derail both your budget and timeline. When planning a major house extension, keeping a few common pitfalls in mind will save you time, stress, and costly rework.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Choosing quotes solely on bottom-line numbers: Low estimates often exclude crucial line items like architectural drawings, waste haul-away, or tie-in stucco work. Always compare detailed, written scopes.
- Overlooking earlier additions: If your home had prior expansions or patio enclosures, they count toward overall lot coverage limits and stormwater allowances.
- Altering layouts after framing starts: Moving a door, window, or plumbing drop mid-build triggers change orders, extra permit inspections, and avoidable delays.
- Forgetting your outdoor drainage: An expanded roofline dumps rainwater in new spots; failing to plan downspouts and yard grading can flood flowerbeds or foundation edges.
- Ignoring roofline aesthetics: A poorly matched roof slope makes an extension look like an awkward afterthought rather than a seamless part of your original architecture.
